syntax.rationale: The page's declaration surface is split across the 'shape of the feature' subsections, and a dimension's slice ends at the next h1, h2 or h3 (scripts/lib/reference-contract.mjs:901), so no single fragment carries the whole surface. This selector maps Step 2, the @container scroll-state() query call form, which is the feature's namesake syntax. Step 1's container-type: scroll-state establishment is mapped to context and Step 3's supported feature and value list to inputs, so all three subsections are covered by a dimension rather than one being left out.

errors.rationale: CSS scroll-state() is declarative with no throwing surface: invalid or unsupported feature/value pairs are dropped by the general CSS error-recovery rules, which the page does not single out, so there is no page-documented error path to map.

context.rationale: Maps Step 1, the container-type: scroll-state declaration that must be established before the query applies, which is the context in which a scroll-state() query is meaningful. It previously pointed at the at-a-glance summary table, which is a digest of the other dimensions rather than a context statement of its own.

securityPrivacy.rationale: scroll-state() is a rendering-only CSS feature: #why explains it replaces JavaScript observer polling with a synchronous paint-pass style, exposing no new script or data surface, and the page documents no security or privacy consideration.

notes: B3 unit (gendn-g8o): the page carried zero id attributes, so six existing headings gained ids (at-a-glance, why, syntax, features, example, browser-support) and nothing else in the page changed. The syntax dimension anchors #syntax (Step 1: establish a scroll-state container), which carries the container-type: scroll-state / container-name declaration in a <pre><code> block; the page's declaration surface is otherwise split across the adjacent 'shape of the feature' subsections — 'Step 2: query with @container scroll-state()' (the query call form) and 'Supported scroll-state features' (#features, the feature/value grammar) — so no single fragment contains the whole surface. CARRIED DIVERGENCES, BOTH SIDES, NEITHER ADJUDICATED: (1) the page's 'Supported scroll-state features' table lists 'both' as a scrollable value, but the live spec's scrollable value list is 'none | top | right | bottom | left | block-start | inline-start | block-end | inline-end | x | y | block | inline' with no 'both' (the spec lists 'both' only for the snapped feature). (2) the page documents three scroll-state features (stuck, snapped, scrollable) — matching the live ChromeStatus summary — but the cited live spec (drafts.csswg.org/css-conditional-5/#scroll-state) additionally defines a fourth feature 'scrolled' (none | top | right | bottom | left | block-start | inline-start | block-end | inline-end | x | y | block | inline) that the page does not mention. (3) the page's 'at a glance' and 'browser support' state the feature shipped in Chrome 149 (desktop + Android), but the live ChromeStatus record 5072263730167808 reports milestone 133 (desktop 133, android 133, webview 133, status 'Enabled by default', last updated 2025-08-25). None of these were fixed in this unit.
